original_value: One of the main barriers for educational games to properly fulfill the specific pedagogical, cultural and technical requirements that are often unique to each situation is the difficulty of reusing and adapting them to different educational contexts. In this sense, open educational games could facilitate reuse and adaptation, once they follow the openness principles. This paper provides a systematic review of open educational games designed specifically for teaching computer programming and computational logic. It has been identified that most authors find the issue of reusing and adapting educational games following the openness philosophy as very important, but even them fail to use open tools in game development. We conclude that most articles recommend using component-based development, reuse and adaptation, but reuse still does not happen in a practical sense. Also, the amount of studies on educational games for teaching programming is low in the scientific literature, and most open educational games available on the Internet are not documented nor have some associated published paper. Thus, reuse and adaptation may even occur, but without scientific documentation and publication.

result.paraphrase: A major obstacle to educational games meeting the pedagogical, cultural, and technical needs that can vary by situation is the difficulty of reusing and adapting them across different educational settings. In this context, open educational games may make reuse and adaptation easier if they adhere to openness principles. This paper presents a systematic review of open educational games developed specifically to teach computer programming and computational logic. It was found that most authors consider reusing and adapting educational games according to the openness philosophy to be very important, yet they still do not use open tools in game development. We conclude that most articles advocate component-based development, reuse, and adaptation, but practical reuse still does not occur. In addition, the number of studies on educational games for teaching programming is low in the scientific literature, and most open educational games available on the Internet are neither documented nor accompanied by a published paper. As a result, reuse and adaptation may occur without scientific documentation or publication.
